lit: to bite down hard and grind the teeth together

use.how: Describes visible, bitter hatred toward a person: 恨得咬牙切齿, or as an adverbial, 咬牙切齿地说. Not for physical effort or mild annoyance.

near.diff: 恨之入骨 states how deep the hatred goes; 咬牙切齿 paints how it shows on the face and in the voice.

cue: Whenever he mentions the man who cheated his family out of their savings, his jaw clenches and he spits out each word. How does he look?

ctx.s: 一提起那个骗子，他就恨得{咬牙切齿}。
ctx.en: Whenever that swindler is mentioned, he hates him so much he grinds his teeth.

ctx.s: 她{咬牙切齿}地说：“我绝不会原谅他。”
ctx.en: She said through gritted teeth: "I will never forgive him."

ctx.s: 被人当众羞辱以后，他{咬牙切齿}，发誓要讨回公道。
ctx.en: After being humiliated in public, he ground his teeth and swore he would get justice.

ctx.s: 你怎么一说到前老板就{咬牙切齿}的？
ctx.en: Why do you grind your teeth every time your old boss comes up?

ctx.s: 小说里，被夺走家产的少年{咬牙切齿}地望着仇人的背影。
ctx.en: In the novel, the boy robbed of his family's property glares with clenched teeth at his enemy's back.

ctx.s: 球迷们对那个吹黑哨的裁判恨得{咬牙切齿}。
ctx.en: The fans loathe that crooked referee with a teeth-grinding hatred.

bad.s: 他{咬牙切齿}地坚持跑完了全程。
bad.en: (meant: he gritted his teeth and kept running to the finish)
bad.why: It expresses hatred, not endurance or grim determination in the face of pain.

bad.s: 听到考试通过的消息，他高兴得{咬牙切齿}。
bad.en: (meant: he was overjoyed to hear he had passed)
bad.why: It can only describe hatred or fury, never happiness.

mean: to swallow one's anger and say nothing
lit: to hold in one's breath and swallow one's voice

use.how: Predicate for someone who takes an insult or injustice in silence, usually from someone more powerful: 只好忍气吞声. Often said with sympathy or as a call to stop.

near.diff: 逆来顺受 is a lasting habit of accepting any mistreatment; 忍气吞声 is holding back one's anger and protest when wronged.

cue: Her manager mocks her in front of everyone, but she needs the job, so she lowers her eyes and never answers back. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 为了保住工作，他只好{忍气吞声}。
ctx.en: To keep his job, he had no choice but to swallow his anger and say nothing.

ctx.s: 房东无理涨租，她却{忍气吞声}，一句话也没说。
ctx.en: The landlord raised the rent for no reason, yet she held her tongue and said not a word.

ctx.s: 你总是{忍气吞声}，别人只会更欺负你。
ctx.en: If you always just take it in silence, people will only bully you more.

ctx.s: 妈妈对女儿说：“受了委屈就说出来，别再{忍气吞声}了。”
ctx.en: The mother told her daughter: "If you've been wronged, speak up. Stop suffering in silence."

ctx.s: 那些年她在婆家{忍气吞声}，从不敢顶一句嘴。
ctx.en: In those years she bore everything silently in her in-laws' house and never dared answer back.

ctx.s: 有了投诉渠道，受欺负的员工不必再{忍气吞声}。
ctx.en: With a way to file complaints, mistreated employees no longer have to suffer in silence.

bad.s: 排队的时候他很有耐心，一直{忍气吞声}。
bad.en: (meant: he waited patiently in the queue)
bad.why: It needs an insult or injustice to swallow; simply waiting patiently is not that.

bad.s: 老师对调皮的学生总是很{忍气吞声}。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher is always patient with naughty pupils)
bad.why: It is about the weaker side enduring humiliation, not tolerance toward those below you, and it is not modified by an adverb of degree.

mean: wishing one had never done it in the first place
lit: to regret what one did at the very beginning

use.how: Predicate, takes no object: 现在悔不当初. Said of one's own earlier choice once its bad results arrive, or as a warning: 别到时候悔不当初.

near.diff: 后悔莫及 stresses that it is too late to undo; 悔不当初 stresses wishing the original choice had been different.

cue: Years ago he quit a stable job, against everyone's advice, for a get-rich scheme, and lost everything. How does he feel about that decision now?

ctx.s: 他炒股赔光了积蓄，{悔不当初}：要是当年没碰股票就好了。
ctx.en: He lost all his savings on the stock market and bitterly regrets ever starting: if only he had never touched shares.

ctx.s: 当年没听父母的劝，如今想起来真是{悔不当初}。
ctx.en: I didn't listen to my parents back then, and now I truly wish I had.

ctx.s: 别等到身体垮了才{悔不当初}。
ctx.en: Don't wait until your health collapses to regret how you lived.

ctx.s: 签合同前一定要看清条款，不然到时候{悔不当初}也晚了。
ctx.en: Read the terms carefully before you sign, or by the time you regret it, it'll be too late.

ctx.s: 你现在{悔不当初}有什么用？还是想想怎么补救吧。
ctx.en: What good does regretting your choice do now? Think about how to fix it.

ctx.s: 搬到那座城市后，他处处不如意，{悔不当初}。
ctx.en: After moving to that city nothing went right, and he wished he had never gone.

bad.s: 我{悔不当初}刚才多吃了一块蛋糕。
bad.en: (meant: I regret eating an extra piece of cake just now)
bad.why: It takes no object, and it is too heavy for a trivial regret about something a moment ago.

bad.s: 听说你出了车祸，我感到{悔不当初}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm sorry to hear about your accident)
bad.why: It is regret for one's own past choice, not sympathy for someone else's misfortune.

mean: to build up a fortune from nothing
lit: to set up a household with empty hands

use.how: Predicate or attributive (白手起家的企业家), said of people who built a business or family wealth with no capital or inheritance.

near.diff: 自力更生 is relying on one's own strength in general; 白手起家 is specifically building a business or fortune from zero.

cue: She arrived in the city with no money and no connections, sold snacks from a cart, and now owns a chain of restaurants. How did she get where she is?

ctx.s: 他的父母{白手起家}，开起了一家小饭馆。
ctx.en: His parents started with nothing and built up a small restaurant.

ctx.s: 这家公司是她一个人{白手起家}创办的。
ctx.en: She founded this company on her own, starting from nothing.

ctx.s: 很多{白手起家}的企业家都特别节俭。
ctx.en: Many self-made entrepreneurs are especially frugal.

ctx.s: 爷爷常说：“咱们家是{白手起家}的，不能忘本。”
ctx.en: Grandpa often says: "Our family started with nothing; we must never forget where we came from."

ctx.s: 你觉得现在的年轻人还有机会{白手起家}吗？
ctx.en: Do you think young people today still have a chance to make it from nothing?

ctx.s: 他二十岁进城，靠一辆三轮车{白手起家}，如今有了自己的物流公司。
ctx.en: He came to the city at twenty and, starting with just a tricycle, now owns a logistics company.

bad.s: 他继承了父亲的公司，从此{白手起家}。
bad.en: (meant: he took over his father's company and started his career)
bad.why: It means starting with nothing; inheriting a company is the opposite.

bad.s: 我{白手起家}，自学会了弹钢琴。
bad.en: (meant: I taught myself piano from scratch)
bad.why: It is about building a business or fortune, not learning a skill from the beginning.

mean: to cling to a method after circumstances have changed
lit: to notch the boat to look for the sword

story.text: A man of Chu was crossing a river when his sword slipped over the side into the water. He quickly cut a notch in the boat and said: this is where my sword fell. When the boat stopped, he went into the water at the notch to look for it. But the boat had moved on, and the sword had not.

use.how: Predicate or after 是: 这是刻舟求剑. Criticises applying an old rule or method to a situation that has moved on.

near.diff: 守株待兔 is waiting passively for a lucky event to repeat; 刻舟求剑 is failing to see that the conditions have changed.

cue: A shop keeps using the sales tricks that worked twenty years ago, though its customers now buy everything on their phones, and wonders why nothing sells.

ctx.s: 市场早就变了，还用十年前的老办法，这不是{刻舟求剑}吗？
ctx.en: The market changed long ago; isn't using the methods of ten years back just looking for the sword by the notch?

ctx.s: 孩子已经长大了，你还用管小孩的办法管他，未免有点{刻舟求剑}。
ctx.en: Your son is grown up; still handling him like a small child is clinging to what no longer applies.

ctx.s: 经理说：“客户的需求每年都在变，我们不能{刻舟求剑}。”
ctx.en: The manager said: "Customers' needs change every year; we can't stick to what worked before."

ctx.s: 法律修改以后，再按旧条文办事就成了{刻舟求剑}。
ctx.en: Once the law has been revised, going by the old provisions is clinging to a changed situation.

ctx.s: 老师讲了{刻舟求剑}的故事，让学生明白情况变了，方法也要变。
ctx.en: The teacher told the story of the notched boat so the pupils would see that when things change, methods must too.

ctx.s: 拿着老地图在新城区找路，简直是{刻舟求剑}。
ctx.en: Finding your way in the new district with an old map is like notching the boat for the sword.

bad.s: 他每天坚持练习，真是{刻舟求剑}。
bad.en: (meant: he perseveres with practice every day)
bad.why: It mocks rigid thinking in a changed situation; it is never praise for persistence.

bad.s: 为了找回钱包，他{刻舟求剑}，把整条街都找遍了。
bad.en: (meant: he searched the whole street for his wallet)
bad.why: It is not about searching hard for a lost object; it criticises outdated methods.

mean: to cover up a wrong in a way that fools only oneself
lit: to cover one's own ears while stealing a bell

story.text: When the Fan family fell, a commoner found a bell of theirs and wanted to carry it off, but it was too big to carry. He struck it with a hammer to break it up, and it rang out loudly. Afraid that others would hear and take it from him, he quickly covered his own ears. The original speaks of a zhong, a large bronze bell; the idiom later replaced it with ling, a bell.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (掩耳盗铃的做法). Criticises hiding a problem or wrongdoing in a way that everyone else can plainly see through.

near.diff: 自欺欺人 is deceiving oneself and others in general; 掩耳盗铃 stresses a clumsy cover-up of something obvious to all.

cue: After a scandal, an official has every critical post about him deleted and carries on as if nobody knows, though the whole city is talking about it.

ctx.s: 删掉差评就以为产品没问题了，简直是{掩耳盗铃}。
ctx.en: Deleting the bad reviews and thinking the product is fine is just fooling yourself.

ctx.s: 他把车门上的刮痕用贴纸一盖，就当没撞过车，这不是{掩耳盗铃}吗？
ctx.en: He covered the scratch on the car door with a sticker and acts as if he never hit anything. Who does he think he's fooling?

ctx.s: 他以为删了聊天记录，别人就不会知道，真是{掩耳盗铃}。
ctx.en: He thought deleting the chat history would keep people from finding out. How self-deceiving.

ctx.s: 把问题报告锁进抽屉，问题并不会消失，这无异于{掩耳盗铃}。
ctx.en: Locking the report in a drawer won't make the problem go away; it's covering your own ears.

ctx.s: 工厂检查前停产，检查组一走又偷偷排污，这种{掩耳盗铃}的做法瞒不了多久。
ctx.en: The factory stops work before inspections and dumps waste once inspectors leave; a cover-up like that won't fool anyone for long.

ctx.s: 老师早就通知你爸妈了，把成绩单藏起来有什么用？别{掩耳盗铃}了。
ctx.en: Your teacher has already told your parents; what good is hiding the report card? Stop fooling yourself.

bad.s: 小偷{掩耳盗铃}，偷走了邻居的自行车。
bad.en: (meant: the thief quietly stole the neighbour's bicycle)
bad.why: It is figurative, for a self-deceiving cover-up; it does not describe an actual theft.

bad.s: 她怕吵，晚上睡觉总是{掩耳盗铃}。
bad.en: (meant: she covers her ears at night because of the noise)
bad.why: It does not mean literally covering one's ears; it mocks a cover-up that fools no one.

mean: actions that lead away from one's own goal
lit: the cart shafts point south while the wheel tracks run north

story.text: Ji Liang heard that the King of Wei meant to attack Handan and hurried to see him. On the road, he said, he had met a man driving north who told him he was going to Chu, in the south. Told he was going the wrong way, the man answered that his horses were good, he had plenty of money and his driver was skilled. The better these were, said Ji Liang, the farther he would get from Chu, just as each attack took the king farther from his aim of leading the states.

use.how: Predicate, often with 与目标 or after 这是: 做法与目标南辕北辙. Criticises means that work against the very goal they are meant to serve.

near.diff: 背道而驰 is going against a principle or another party; 南辕北辙 is one's own actions defeating one's own goal.

cue: Someone says he is saving hard for a flat, yet every week he spends more on online shopping and wonders why the savings never grow.

ctx.s: 想减肥却天天吃夜宵，这不是{南辕北辙}吗？
ctx.en: You want to lose weight but eat a late-night snack every day. Isn't that working against yourself?

ctx.s: 方向错了，再努力也是{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: If the direction is wrong, the harder you try, the farther you get from your goal.

ctx.s: 老师对家长说：“想让孩子爱上读书，却天天逼他抄书，这是{南辕北辙}啊。”
ctx.en: The teacher told the parents: "You want him to love reading, yet you make him copy out books every day. That leads the opposite way."

ctx.s: 公司要提高效率，却增加了一堆审批手续，做法与目标{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: The company wants more efficiency but added a pile of approval steps; the means run counter to the goal.

ctx.s: 他一心想当医生，却把时间都花在打游戏上，真可谓{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: He is set on becoming a doctor, yet spends all his time on video games: every step takes him further from his goal.

ctx.s: 为了练口语而只背单词表，恐怕是{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: Only memorising word lists to improve your speaking is probably moving away from what you want.

bad.s: 我家在南边，公司在北边，每天上班{南辕北辙}。
bad.en: (meant: my home and office are far apart, so my commute is long)
bad.why: It is a figure for self-defeating actions, not a literal description of distance or direction.

bad.s: 他{南辕北辙}地跑遍了全国。
bad.en: (meant: he travelled all over the country)
bad.why: It does not mean travelling widely all over the country; it is about self-defeating actions.

mean: professing a love for something one actually fears

story.text: Lord Ye, named Zigao, loved dragons. He had them on his belt hooks and his vessels and carved throughout his house. A real dragon in heaven heard of it and came down. It put its head in at his window and trailed its tail into his hall. Lord Ye saw it, turned and fled, so terrified he lost his wits. What he loved was not dragons, but things that looked like dragons.

use.how: Predicate or after 是: 这是叶公好龙. Said of someone who praises or claims to want something but shrinks from it when it really arrives.

near.diff: 口是心非 is saying one thing and meaning another about anything; 叶公好龙 is claiming to love something and fleeing it once it is real.

cue: For years your friend has talked about wanting a dog, but when you offer him a puppy to keep, he backs away and makes excuses.

ctx.s: 他总说喜欢狗，可朋友的狗一靠近他就躲，真是{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: He always says he loves dogs, yet he hides whenever a friend's dog comes near. All talk.

ctx.s: 你天天说想去爬雪山，机会来了又不敢去，不会是{叶公好龙}吧？
ctx.en: You keep saying you want to climb a snow mountain, then the chance comes and you won't go. Do you really want it?

ctx.s: 公司口口声声欢迎提意见，真有人提了却不高兴，这不是{叶公好龙}吗？
ctx.en: The company keeps saying it welcomes criticism, then gets annoyed when someone gives it. Isn't that loving the dragon only in pictures?

ctx.s: 他自称热爱大自然，可一到野外就嫌脏嫌累，朋友笑他{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: He claims to love nature, but outdoors he complains about the dirt and the effort; his friends tease him for it.

ctx.s: 有些人嘴上爱谈创新，真要改变时却百般阻挠，不过是{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: Some people love to talk about innovation but block every real change; their love is only for show.

ctx.s: 说重视人才不难，能不能容下有主见的人才是关键，否则就是{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: Saying you value talent is easy; whether you can tolerate people with their own views is what counts. Otherwise it's empty love.

bad.s: 他从小就特别喜欢龙，是个{叶公好龙}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he has genuinely loved dragons since childhood)
bad.why: It mocks a love that is false; it never describes a real fondness.

bad.s: 她{叶公好龙}，一直在默默地学画画。
bad.en: (meant: she quietly loves painting and keeps practising)
bad.why: It means professing a love one backs away from, not a hidden passion one pursues.

mean: to fill a place without the skill for it
lit: to make up the number as a sham player of the yu, a reed mouth organ

story.text: King Xuan of Qi liked to hear the yu, a reed mouth organ, played by three hundred musicians together. A man known as Mr Nanguo, who could not play, asked to join the band and was paid like the others. When King Xuan died, his son King Min preferred to hear the players one at a time, and Mr Nanguo ran away.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (滥竽充数的人). Criticises an unqualified person hidden in a group, or modestly said of oneself: 我只是来滥竽充数的.

near.diff: 鱼目混珠 is passing off fakes as genuine, often goods; 滥竽充数 is an unqualified person filling a place among capable ones.

cue: Asked to join the office choir for a show, you stand at the back and mouth the words because you can't really sing. How do you describe your part?

ctx.s: 我唱歌不好，在合唱团里只是{滥竽充数}。
ctx.en: I'm not a good singer; in the choir I'm just making up the numbers.

ctx.s: “你这次也上台演出？”“别提了，我就是去{滥竽充数}的。”
ctx.en: "You're performing too this time?" "Don't ask. I'm only there to make up the numbers."

ctx.s: 球队人手不够，连不会踢球的人也来{滥竽充数}。
ctx.en: The team was short of players, so even people who can't play football were brought in to fill places.

ctx.s: 招聘一定要严格，不能让{滥竽充数}的人混进来。
ctx.en: Hiring must be strict; we can't let people who aren't up to the job slip in.

ctx.s: 这本论文集里有几篇明显是{滥竽充数}的。
ctx.en: Several papers in this collection are obviously just there to fill it out.

ctx.s: 实行个人考核以后，那些{滥竽充数}的员工就藏不住了。
ctx.en: Once individual assessments began, the employees who were only filling seats had nowhere to hide.

bad.s: 这家店的东西又多又便宜，真是{滥竽充数}。
bad.en: (meant: this shop has lots of cheap things)
bad.why: It is about an unqualified person filling a place, not about a large quantity of goods.

bad.s: 他技术最好，是乐队里{滥竽充数}的主力。
bad.en: (meant: he is the most skilled, key member of the band)
bad.why: It means lacking the skill for one's place, so it contradicts calling him the best.

mean: to imitate others clumsily and look ridiculous

story.text: The beauty Xi Shi had a pain in her chest and frowned as she walked through her village, and even so she looked lovely. An ugly woman of the village saw this, thought it beautiful, and went about clutching her chest and frowning too. The rich shut their gates and stayed in; the poor took their families and kept away. She saw that the frown was beautiful, but not why. In Zhuangzi she is only an ugly neighbour; the name Dong Shi came later.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (东施效颦之作). Criticises copying someone without the qualities that made it work; also said modestly of one's own imitation.

near.diff: 邯郸学步 is imitating so much that one loses one's own ability; 东施效颦 is imitating badly and looking ridiculous.

cue: A small start-up copies every rule and ritual of a giant tech firm, though it has ten staff, and ends up looking absurd and getting less done.

ctx.s: 他学偶像在台上耍酷，动作却僵硬别扭，简直是{东施效颦}。
ctx.en: He tried to act cool on stage like his idol, but his moves were so stiff it was just a clumsy copy.

ctx.s: 写作要有自己的风格，一味模仿名家只会{东施效颦}。
ctx.en: A writer needs a style of their own; blindly imitating the masters just looks clumsy.

ctx.s: 小公司照搬大公司的管理制度，往往{东施效颦}，反而乱了套。
ctx.en: When small firms copy big companies' management systems wholesale, it often backfires and throws everything into chaos.

ctx.s: 你学他那样说话，不觉得有点{东施效颦}吗？
ctx.en: Copying the way he talks, don't you think you look a bit ridiculous?

ctx.s: 这部电影模仿好莱坞大片，特效却很粗糙，被观众批评为{东施效颦}。
ctx.en: The film imitates Hollywood blockbusters, but its effects are crude, and audiences dismissed it as a clumsy copy.

ctx.s: 他谦虚地说：“我这幅画是{东施效颦}，跟齐白石比还差得远。”
ctx.en: He said modestly: "This painting of mine is a clumsy imitation; it's nowhere near Qi Baishi."

bad.s: 他虚心向老师学习，{东施效颦}，进步很快。
bad.en: (meant: he learned humbly by imitating his teacher and improved fast)
bad.why: It mocks imitation that makes one look foolish; it cannot praise successful learning.

bad.s: 听到坏消息，她{东施效颦}，一脸愁容。
bad.en: (meant: she frowned when she heard the bad news)
bad.why: It is not a description of frowning; it is about copying someone clumsily.
